title: Butter Chicken
subtitle: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready
description: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Rinse and start the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse basmati until water runs clear. Simmer with 1:1.5 rice-to-water and a pinch of salt 15 minutes; rest covered 10 minutes off heat. Fluff and hold at 200°F in a covered hotel pan.

steps.title: Build the yogurt marinade
steps.instruction: Stir yogurt with garam masala, cumin, half the garlic and ginger, and salt until smooth. Toss cubed chicken until coated; marinate at least 30 minutes in the fridge.

steps.title: Sear the chicken in batches
steps.instruction: Heat 2 tbsp butter in a heavy pot over medium-high. Sear chicken in single layers until golden on the edges — not cooked through. Transfer to a hotel pan.

steps.title: Sweat the aromatics
steps.instruction: Lower heat to medium. Add remaining butter and diced onion; cook 8 minutes until soft and translucent. Add remaining garlic and ginger; stir 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the makhani sauce
steps.instruction: Pour in crushed tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes, scraping the fond. Stir in cream and simmer 5 more minutes until the sauce coats a spoon and looks deep orange-red.

steps.title: Finish chicken to 165°F
steps.instruction: Return seared chicken and any juices. Simmer gently 12–15 minutes until thickest pieces read 165°F. Stir occasionally so nothing sticks on the bottom.

steps.title: Balance the sauce
steps.instruction: Taste for salt and a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes are sharp. Add a splash of cream if the sauce looks broken or grainy. Keep at a gentle simmer — do not boil hard after cream is in.

steps.title: Hold through call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop, hold the pot covered on the warm side of the range at 140°F. Stir in a tablespoon of cream before service if the surface tightens.

steps.title: Serve Butter Chicken for the crew
steps.instruction: Mound fluffy basmati on sheet trays or bowls, then ladle saucy chicken over the rice. Finish with cilantro. Keep extra sauce in a labeled cambro for seconds.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers
steps.instruction: Cool chicken and rice in shallow pans within two hours. Reheat chicken to 165°F next shift; refresh rice with a splash of water.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Butter Chicken with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Butter Chicken on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Rich tomato butter sauce, naan-ready. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
